source.title: On the Impact of Knowledge Distillation for Model Interpretability
source.authors: Hyeongrok Han; Siwon Kim; Hyun-Soo Choi; Sungroh Yoon

page_placements.theme: Training regime, data, objective and architecture shift unit-level concept alignment in vision, audio and genomic models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures interpretability of vision and NLP models, but it does not test the claim's neuron-pole job shares, explanations on held-out activating examples, or the other specified versions.
record.gate_note: The study counts convolutional units aligned with labeled concepts using network dissection. Those counts do not measure the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs, and the study does not test neuron explanations on activations they were not written from. Its results are recorded as related interpretability findings, not as tests of a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study counts Broden network-dissection concept detectors in ResNet-18 and a few other CNNs, and compares scratch, knowledge-distilled and label-smoothed training. It never addresses neuron-pole job shares (V1, V2), the cat-and-car neuron (V3), neuron-based attribution graphs (V5), or how well explanations predict activations (V6, V7). V4 names architecture, regularization and tools as causes. The label-smoothing result touches regularization only loosely: the varied factor is the training signal, and the outcome is a raw detector count (unique and total over 512-ish units, with no denominator stated), not a share of interpretable neurons. The study also does not compare explanation tools or architecture generations in a way that bears on V4. It is recorded as a related finding, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that KD improves both accuracy and interpretability (more concept detectors, more object-centric activations). They attribute this to class-similarity information from the teacher, and report consistent results across KD methods, datasets, interpretability measures and an NLP (BERT/SST) task.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses knowledge distillation and network dissection, along with attribution-based measures; it does not audit neuron poles or test neuron explanations on held-out activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies KD method, temperature and alpha, network architecture, layer, activation quantile, and IoU threshold; it reports that these settings affect detector counts.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 layer-4 network-dissection counts: vanilla KD gives 312 total and 166 unique detectors, versus 275/162 for scratch and 219/153 for label smoothing (Table 1). Other KD methods give 283–316 total detectors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training regime (distillation vs label-smoothing regularization) changes how many CNN units align with labeled Broden concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 11 reports unique and total detector counts for ResNet-34/50, MobileNet v2 and EfficientNet-b2, scratch vs KD. KD is higher in each case, but counts are not normalised by unit number.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The KD increase in concept-detector counts holds across several CNN architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The study's concept-detector count is not a measure of neuron-pole job shares or of how accurately explanations predict firing on held-out activations. The reported detector-count averages over three initializations have no stated error bars or dispersion.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported attribution and interpretability results, including five-band scores, DiffROAR, loss-gradient visualizations, and SST attribution scores, are omitted because they use different interpretation measures and do not test the claim's specified neuron-pole versions.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares (one job, two related jobs, not understood).
Pole shares in other language models, dense or MoE, at scale.

Whether the interpretable-neuron share rises with better tools and modern architectures, and the 5%→99% InceptionV1-size estimates. Regularization is touched only via label smoothing lowering detector counts, and no shares are given.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows are correctly linked to none, and cannot_determine is appropriate. Detector counts are raw counts; the number of layer-4 units is not stated in the text, so no share can be read. The record's relation 'discusses' is generous, since the paper never refers to the claim. T6 is the right tranche.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B pole shares and the proportions with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not yet understood.
Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or model scale up to trillions of parameters.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, or explanation tools account for interpretable-neuron shares, and the stated estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Whether attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where a neuron fires on other examples.
Automated scores for neuron explanations simulated on new text.

relation.reason: Topical paper on KD and unit interpretability via network dissection. It predates the claim and tests none of its versions.

tranche.reason: Counts Broden network-dissection concept detectors under scratch, KD and LS training. No test of neuron-pole job shares, the cat-and-car neuron, attribution graphs or whether explanations predict firing. Shares of all units are not reported.

source_check.notes: All six rows match Table 1 (ResNet-18 last conv layer, mean of three runs). Loosely relevant to V4's 'regularization' factor: at fixed architecture and tool, LS lowers and KD raises layer-4 concept-detector counts. These are counts, not shares, and no tool or architecture comparison is made, so leaving the rows unlinked is defensible.
